themes_detail.label: Animal Invasion in Parks
themes_detail.summary: Parks across Riverdale/Fieldston are experiencing an unprecedented surge in animal complaints this week, with 4 reports filed vs. a baseline of 0.4 per week—a 967% spike (z-score: 7.49)—suggesting a potential wildlife management crisis or seasonal migration problem requiring immediate investigation.
evidence: 4 animal-in-park complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
967% increase represents highest statistical anomaly in district (z-score: 7.49, severity: high)
Community Board has standing request to 'reconstruct or upgrade a park or amenity' with new maintenance equipment, suggesting parks infrastructure may be inadequate to manage wildlife
reporting_angles: What species are being reported and why are they appearing now? Talk to Parks Dept and local residents about sightings.
Are park conditions (trash, maintenance, lighting) making them attractive to animals? Connect to CB's unfunded park upgrade requests.

themes_detail.label: Construction Surge and Safety Risks
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints spiked this week to 11 reports vs. a baseline of 4.8 per week—a 132% increase (z-score: 4.81)—coinciding with 323 total DOB permits filed in 90 days (199 alterations), suggesting potential safety compliance or contractor conduct issues.
evidence: 11 general construction/plumbing complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.8 weekly baseline (132% spike, z-score: 4.81)
323 DOB permits filed in last 90 days (199 alterations, 66 new buildings), highest activity level in district
Complaints filed across multiple permit types suggests systemic compliance or contractor behavior issues, not isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Are contractors operating without proper permits or insurance? Cross-reference 311 complaints with DOB enforcement records.
Are residents being displaced or experiencing noise/safety hazards? Reach out to affected building addresses from complaint log.

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Dangling and damaged street signs are spiking across the district—3 dangling signs last week (up 1100% from 0.2 baseline) and 6 damaged signs 2 weeks ago (up 336%)—indicating potential systemic street furniture failure or deferred maintenance affecting pedestrian safety.
evidence: 3 dangling street signs reported LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score: 4.16, severity: high)
6 damaged street signs reported 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.4 weekly average (336% spike, z-score: 3.51, severity: high)
Community Board has unfunded recurring request to 'improve traffic and pedestrian safety,' suggesting infrastructure maintenance is chronic problem
reporting_angles: Map the locations of dangling/damaged signs—are they concentrated in specific neighborhoods or corridors?
How long has DOT known about these hazards? Request maintenance records and response times from city agency.

themes_detail.label: Food Safety and Vendor Enforcement Gaps
themes_detail.summary: Food establishment complaints and vendor enforcement issues spiked dramatically last week (4 food complaints, up 357% from 0.9 baseline) and 2 weeks ago (3 vendor enforcement complaints, up 500% from 0.5 baseline), suggesting potential health code violations or inadequate regulatory oversight.
evidence: 4 food establishment complaints filed LAST WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average (357% spike, z-score: 4.0, severity: high)
3 vendor enforcement complaints filed 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% spike, z-score: 3.54, severity: high)
Convergence of food safety and enforcement signals suggests either new unlicensed vendors or existing establishments falling out of compliance
reporting_angles: Which restaurants or food vendors are generating complaints? Request inspection records from DOHMH.
Are street vendors operating illegally? Interview residents and business owners about enforcement visibility.

themes_detail.label: Pigeon Infestation Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary pigeon condition complaints surged 2 weeks ago with 3 reports vs. a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 1100% spike (z-score: 6.35)—suggesting deteriorating sanitation or failure to implement pest management in public spaces.
evidence: 3 unsanitary pigeon condition complaints filed 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35, severity: high)
Overlaps with animal-in-park surge this week, suggesting broader wildlife/pest management challenge across district
437 unsanitary condition complaints over 90 days (top 7 complaint type) indicates general sanitation may be deteriorating
reporting_angles: Visit sites with multiple pigeon complaints—are parks or public spaces accumulating trash or food waste?
Interview Parks Dept or Sanitation about pigeon population management strategy and funding.
